bib.title: 3D Object Representations for Fine-Grained Categorization
bib.venue: 2013 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision Workshops (ICCVW)

question: Does lifting 2D object representations (SPM, BubbleBank) to 3D object space improve fine-grained car categorization, and what dataset tests it?
hypothesis: Distinctive features of a fine-grained category are most naturally represented in 3D object space, so 3D representations should beat 2D ones and generalise across viewpoints.
contributions: Lift SPM and BubbleBank to 3D in both appearance and location
New dataset of 207 fine-grained categories (BMW-10 and car-197)
Ultra-wide baseline matching with the 3D representation
First 3D reconstruction of a fine-grained category

method.summary: Estimate rough 3D geometry of a car by matching to 41 CAD models with HOG one-vs-all linear SVMs over 1,008 viewpoint/coarse-category combinations, then pool RootSIFT features on rectified patches in 3D object space (SPM-3D, BB-3D) and classify with one-vs-all linear SVMs. Also introduces the BMW-10 and car-197 datasets.
method.task: fine-grained car classification; ultra-wide baseline matching; 3D reconstruction

datasets.name: car-197
datasets.source: Class list crawled from a car website (cars made since 1990), deduplicated by perceptual hashing, 197 sampled; candidate images from Flickr, Google, Bing, deduplicated; verified on Amazon Mechanical Turk with Get Another Label (GAL) worker-quality model; AMT bounding boxes; final dedup on cropped boxes. Licence not stated.
datasets.preprocessing: Cropped to bounding box, max dimension scaled to 300 pixels

datasets.name: BMW-10
datasets.preprocessing: Cropped, max dimension 300 px; flipped variant doubles training images

datasets.name: Synthetic CAD renders
datasets.source: 41 CAD models of cars rendered at 36 azimuths, 4 elevations, 10 random backgrounds

models.architecture: hand-engineered features (RootSIFT, LLC coding or bubble responses) with 3D pooling and linear SVM

other.hypotheses: 3 viewpoint/coarse-category hypotheses x 3 CAD models each
other.coarse categories: sedan, SUV, coupe, convertible, pickup, hatchback, station wagon

models.name: SPM (LLC), BB, HOG, KDES, PB(mvDPM), structDPM

training.regularisation: C chosen from 1e-6..1e10 by 25-fold cross-validation (small-scale); constant C=1e10 (large-scale)
training.seeds: training images randomly sampled and fixed across methods in the amount-of-data experiment; number of seeds not stated

other.geometry classifiers: HOG + one-vs-all linear SVM, 1,008 viewpoint/coarse-category classes

limits: No train/test split sizes for car-197 or BMW-10 appear in the paper; implementation details and the class list are in supplementary material not in the PDF.

car-197 is 197 classes here; the 3D representation lost to plain 2D SPM on car-197 (69.5% vs 67.6%), which the authors attribute to underrepresentation of coarse categories such as large pickups in the CAD models.
Rigid objects only (cars); needs CAD models per coarse category.
Reconstruction result is qualitative and incomplete, with spurious points in textureless regions.
Hand-engineered pre-deep-learning features; accuracies are not comparable to later CNN results.
Single run per cell with no variance reported.
